language_task: Pick up the spoon and place it into the box.
outcome_evidence: The first lift loses the spoon onto the table beside the box (frames 48–52, ceiling and wrist_left). The robot retries, lifts the spoon again (frames 84–90, wrist_left), and releases it into the blue box (frames 108–112, wrist_right). The spoon remains inside after withdrawal through frame 132 (ceiling), confirming completion despite the earlier failed retention.

failure_annotations.explanation: After visibly lifting the spoon in frames 44–47 (wrist_left), the gripper loses retention beginning at frame 48; the spoon falls and rests on the tabletop outside the box by frames 50–52 (ceiling and wrist_left). The gripper moves away without it, preventing this transfer from completing; task-directed return begins at frame 56.
failure_annotations.recovery: Return to the spoon’s updated position, align the fingers around its handle, regrasp, and verify retention with a short lift before transferring it into the box; no human intervention is needed.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The spoon falls onto the tabletop and remains accessible; no damage or disruption to other objects is visible.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The spoon remains on the open tabletop beside the box and can be reacquired directly without environmental resetting or human intervention.
